key_insight: A three-variable stochastic model links stable large-scale circulation to one relaxational mode and two damped oscillatory modes, with turbulence continually exciting the oscillations.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a compact framework for interpreting coherent circulation, oscillations, and rare flow reversals in buoyancy-driven turbulent systems.
method: Derive coupled stochastic equations for circulation angular velocity and a dipolar temperature field from the Boussinesq equations.
Linearize around stable circulation states to identify decay modes and turnover-rate-controlled oscillations.
Compare predicted modes and Rayleigh-number scalings with thin-disk convection experiments.
evidence_signal: Thin-disk experiments resolve the relaxational and oscillatory modes and show their predicted Rayleigh-number scalings.
watch_item: Validation described in the abstract is limited to a thin-disk cell; transfer to other geometries and quantitative prediction of rare transitions require further testing.
paper_title: Stable eigenmodes of the Large-scale circulation in Turbulent Convection
